sentences.Hawa har hatt språkpraksis på hotellet i: Hawa has had a language placement at the hotel for a year.
sentences.Nå vil hotellsjefen snakke med henne, og: Now the hotel manager wants to talk to her, and Hawa is a bit nervous as she goes to the manager's office.
sentences.Hun håper at hun ikke har gjort noe feil: She hopes that she hasn't done anything wrong, or that any of the guests have complained about her.
Hi, Hawa! Good that you could come.
sentences.Nei da! Jeg vil bare snakke litt med deg: No, not at all! I just want to have a little talk with you. Are you enjoying your language placement here?
sentences.Ja, jeg har lært mye norsk, og jeg trive: Yes, I've learned a lot of Norwegian, and I get on really well with my colleagues.
sentences.Det er godt å høre. Vi er veldig fornøyd: That's good to hear. We're very happy with you too. I have an offer for you. If you'd like a proper paid job here, you can cover for Nora for a year. She is going on parental leave.
sentences.Er det sant? Jeg drømmer jo om å få en j: Really? I've been dreaming of getting a job.
sentences.Ja, jeg håper at du sier ja. Det er en m: Yes, I hope you'll say yes. It's a temporary position.
sentences.Jeg sier JA! Hvordan er arbeidstida?: I say YES! What are the working hours like?
sentences.Det er skiftarbeid. Noen dager jobber du: It's shift work. Some days you work during the day, and other days you work in the evening. Perhaps you can carry on going to the Norwegian course a few days a week. If you're going to work at the hotel, it's important that you learn more Norwegian too.
sentences.Det høres perfekt ut. Nå ble jeg veldig: That sounds perfect. I'm so happy now. Thank you so much!
sentences.Bare hyggelig! Vi kan ha et møte senere: You're welcome! We can have a meeting later to sign the employment contract.
Hawa's boss wants to talk to her.
sentences.Hun gruer seg litt, for hun er redd for: She is a bit worried, because she is afraid that someone has complained about her.
sentences.Sjefen hennes spør om hun trives på jobb: Her boss asks if she is enjoying work.
sentences.Hawa svarer at hun trives med kollegaene: Hawa answers that she gets on well with her colleagues, and that she has learned a lot of Norwegian.
sentences.Sjefen sier at de er fornøyde med henne: The boss says that they are happy with her at the hotel.
sentences.Hun spør henne om hun vil ha ett års vik: She asks her if she would like a one-year temporary post.
sentences.Det er ikke en fast stilling, men Hawa b: It isn't a permanent position, but Hawa is very happy because she dreams of getting a job.
sentences.Jeg var på hotellet på språkpraksis i gå: I was at the hotel on my language placement yesterday, and the boss called me into the office.
sentences.Hun sa at hun er fornøyd med meg, og spu: She said that she is happy with me, and asked if I would like to work as a temp at the hotel.
A colleague is going on maternity leave.
sentences.Det er en midlertidig stilling, og jeg k: It's a temporary position, and maybe I can get a permanent job later.
sentences.Jeg kan gå på norskkurs noen dager i uka: I can go to the Norwegian course a few days a week, because it's shift work.
